Yes. I read the four requested web resources, all of `src`, the README, and `AGENT_SPEC.md`. **Several implementation issues explain this run’s zero evidence.**

1. **The repeat guard blocks legitimate reauthentication.**  
   [planner.py:584](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/planner.py:584) remembers state/action pairs across the entire investigation. When an expired session returns to an identical login page, filling the username or clicking login is treated as a forbidden repeat. This explains mail steps 19–24 and tender steps 17–24. Reset repetition tracking after meaningful progress or scope it to consecutive unsuccessful attempts. Failed actions also enter the set before execution.

2. **Document clicks cannot reliably produce readable evidence.**  
   [planner.py:438](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/planner.py:438) clicks links but never captures downloads, follows new tabs, or parses selected files. Observation only reads the main document, excluding iframe contents. The repeated CSV clicks in tender steps 15–16 are consistent with this gap, although the logs do not prove a download occurred. The challenge explicitly includes iframe and ZIP obstacles. [Challenge description](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md)

3. **A slider drag is reported as successful without checking its effect.**  
   [planner.py:381](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/planner.py:381) performs a mouse gesture and returns success without verifying the resulting value or unlocked state. Your ERP and mail sliders remain at `0` afterward. The precise reason the gesture failed requires reproduction; the missing outcome check is definite.

4. **The model cannot see whether fields are disabled.**  
   [planner.py:222](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/planner.py:222) exposes populated and checked states but omits enabled, disabled, and read-only states. ERP therefore tries filling the locked receipt field and wastes ten seconds. Include actual editability, including disabled fieldset ancestry, and reject unavailable controls promptly.

5. **One model timeout permanently stops an investigator.**  
   [planner.py:570](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/planner.py:570) breaks immediately on any model exception. That explains ERP stopping after 13 steps. Add bounded retries for transient failures within the remaining deadline; the platform also recommends retrying failed model calls. [Model guidance](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start.md)

6. **The completion summary incorrectly implies success.**  
   [__main__.py:35](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/__main__.py:35) counts every returned dictionary as completed, including timeouts and exhausted step budgets, then exits successfully if any dictionary exists. Consequently, “4 completed, 0 failed” conceals four unsuccessful investigations. Return explicit outcome statuses. Per-worker evidence counts also currently report the shared ledger’s total.

7. **The investigation budget and memory are insufficient.**  
   [planner.py:18](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/planner.py:18) allows only 24 actions, including credential entry, consent, recovery, and evidence recording. Your customer worker spends almost everything on these obstacles. Each model turn receives only the last action result and recorded evidence—no navigation history or retained findings—which encourages repeated detours. Increasing the limit alone will not fix the underlying loops.

8. **Evidence can be silently lost.**  
   [evidence.py:33](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/evidence.py:33) discards records beyond 60; prompts include only the latest 30, and recorded quotes are truncated to 500 characters. Evidence exists only in memory and is never exported. This makes later resolution and debugging fragile.

**Competition readiness:** the README accurately describes an exploration MVP. There is no implemented material resolution, pricing, answer validation, or TAN submission flow. Even successful exploration would currently end without a scored answer; the rules require signing and submission, including for partial bids. [Bid rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md#bid-rules)

**Fair play:** I found no hardcoded scenario answers or autonomous crawler in `src`; model-directed assignments and navigation fit the published rules. One defensive gap remains: [browser.py:35](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/src/rfq_agent/browser.py:35) launches Chromium whenever CDP configuration is absent, even during a run. It should fail explicitly in run mode, because starting your own sandbox browser is prohibited. [Fair-play rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)

I would fix repetition tracking, selected-document handling, and verification outcomes first. I made no edits and did not start a scouting or scored run; these findings come from source review and your logs.

**Keep the current foundation; don’t restart from scratch.** Runtime URLs, credentials, model-selected navigation, and source-quoted evidence are the right basis for unfamiliar websites. The remaining risk comes from missing workflow stages and interface capabilities.

I strengthened adaptation by adding:

- Accessible labels and more ARIA controls.
- Selection of observed dropdown options.
- Model-requested screenshots and tab switching.
- Reading beyond the first page-text chunk.
- Persistent investigation notes and explicit guidance to follow evidence across sites.

**All 12 regression tests pass**, including synthetic tests with unfamiliar labels, IDs, custom controls, and long pages.

That establishes browser mechanics—not final-run robustness. Before competition readiness, we still need shared evidence-gap tracking and reassignment, authority/date/revision resolution, deterministic pricing, answer validation, and signed submission. We should validate those against held-out synthetic scenarios with different layouts **and different distributions of facts across sites**.

I documented the workflow, known limitations, and validation criteria in [ROBUSTNESS.md](/Users/vladmoroshan/Desktop/Repos/EHL_Finale/docs/ROBUSTNESS.md). My recommendation is to evolve this implementation around that workflow, rather than keep tuning it to public-site logs.
